selected.text: As to thy sighs and lamentations and thy state of agitation and distress, thou art justified. However, it behooveth thee to serve the Threshold of the All-Merciful with the utmost assurance, steadfastness and certitude, for these trials and tribulations are in the path of the All-Glorious
selected.reason: Validates lamentation and distress before inviting renewed service.

selected.text: Though Khidr broke the vessel on the sea, … In Khidr's breaking there were mysteries. … God saith in His mighty Book: "And We will surely try you with something of fear and hunger and loss of wealth and lives and fruits; but give glad tidings to the patient." And likewise He saith: "Those who patiently persevere will truly receive a reward without measure
selected.reason: Invokes Khidr's broken vessel and Quranic patience as a distinctive account of hidden wisdom.

selected.text: During the days when Akka was in confusion and the whirlwind of tests was violent, and a rumor persisted that they were about to banish us to a remote place, we were engaged in planting these trees and flowers, and laying out this garden
selected.reason: Describes planting a garden during threatening rumors, giving a concrete constructive response.

selected.text: Many believe themselves to be courageous, but the battlefield of tests and trials will prove whether they have the real strength to stand firm. … In Persia some believers who claimed to have Faith in Baha'u'llah fell away when they were tested. On the other hand, some who thought themselves weak, proved to be heroes and martyrs
selected.reason: Shows that people who thought themselves weak could prove courageous in actual trials.

selected.text: This is one of the tests of God. That is why Jesus told all people to supplicate and beseech God that He might not let them fall into these tests. (God does not tempt us, --the devil tempts--God tests us.)
selected.reason: Distinguishes testing from temptation in a reported conversation and preserves its status.

selected.text: And today all are tried by that for which I have evinced patience in the path of God and am well-pleased with His decree -- dwelling in stillness upon the mountain -- that the souls may be tested and the hearts purified by the ordinance of that noble verse: "Say: I ask of you no reward, save love for the near of kin." Men follow the decree of kinship with the Messenger of God -- this is the command of God and the wondrousness of His wisdom. "Do men imagine that they will be left alone ... ?" And the Imam said for strengthening -- . By my life, the Cause hath now reached all, and all are tried this very day. Whoso grieveth for my plight and can do no more than this, hath verily
selected.reason: Recognizes compassion from someone able only to grieve, broadening the forms of solidarity.

selected.text: By My life, thy return is better than the acceptance of one who was not adorned with the ornament of permission. Thy Lord is the best Helper, the best Informed, the best Knower.
selected.reason: Values an obedient return over an unauthorized visit, qualifying heroic-seeming action.

selected.text: For nigh upon forty years We have forbidden the servants, through compassionate counsels and wise exhortations, from corruption, conflict and contention. This purpose, through the absolute Divine Will and His aid, gained influence in the realms of Persia, to such an extent that when they heard evil, they spoke good; when they witnessed ugliness, they showed forth beauty; when they were slain, they interceded on behalf of their slayers. Nevertheless, neither from the government nor from the people did anyone take notice.
selected.reason: Links decades of suffering with explicit prohibition of conflict and corruption.

selected.text: the physical frame, it is afflicted with countless trials. And if you ask about the spirit, it is in the heights of joy and delight. In the path of God, I have never complained of tribulation. Rather, in the love of the All-Merciful, I have grown accustomed to trials and afflictions just as an infant is accustomed to its mother's breast
selected.reason: Distinguishes bodily affliction from spiritual joy without erasing the former.

selected.text: Your days shall come - be not disheartened. These are days of wisdom and kindness - observe them carefully.
selected.reason: Makes wisdom and kindness explicit responsibilities during discouraging days.

selected.text: By Thy glory, O my God! I am content with all of this, but Thine enemies rejoice therein and mock Thy loved ones, and because of this mine eyes weep and my heart bleeds and my liver is consumed
selected.reason: Distinguishes accepting one's own trials from grief over cruelty to others.

selected.text: Thou hast endured many hardships in the path of God. No matter hath been or shall be hidden from God, and no service hath been or shall be lost.
selected.reason: Assures a weary servant that hardship and service are not forgotten.

selected.text: Whatsoever befalleth in this Day the sincere ones, the assured ones, the steadfast ones, and the firm ones hath not been due to error or transgression.
selected.reason: States directly that these sufferers' afflictions were not due to error or transgression.

selected.text: O friends! The most tender and sensitive heart hath endured all grievous trials, that perchance some souls might be sanctified from the allusions and veils of all who dwell in the realms of creation and turn toward the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Describes the sufferer's heart as tender and sensitive rather than emotionally invulnerable.

selected.text: How strange it is, O my God, that they remain heedless of the descent of this calamity and show little awareness that this tribulation is the consequence of their actions. For justice demands retribution for crimes and sins, and reward for those of purity, chastity, obedience and submission. They see that this bitter tree has grown from the blood that was shed by the hands of every oppressor and ignorant one, and that this poisonous plant has sprouted from seeds sown by the hands of every treacherous and tyrannical one.
selected.reason: Attributes a calamity to treacherous human deeds, preserving moral responsibility.

selected.text: From this blessed verse it is clear and evident that whoever travels the divine path, the wealthy become poor, not the poor wealthy - it works in reverse … poverty, abasement, tribulation and trials are essential requirements of sacrifice in God's path
selected.reason: Challenges any expectation that religious sacrifice necessarily produces material wealth.

selected.text: For the mighty winds of tests are blowing today - the Hands of the Cause must not sit idle for a moment nor become engaged in any other affairs until the storm of trials subsides, the turbulence of tests becomes still
selected.reason: Assigns active responsibility to the Hands of the Cause during a historical crisis.

selected.text: In the blessed verse He says: "We seized them with lesser punishment before the greater punishment, that they might return." But alas, alas! Where is awakening and where is awareness? Heedlessness has so encompassed them that warning does not awaken them … Do you think that you will enter Paradise while yet there has not come to you the like of what came to those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: 'When will the help of God come
selected.reason: Explores scriptural cries for help and the possibility of awakening through adversity.

selected.text: Concerning what thou didst write about several individuals from the Sikh community, that one of them is very attracted and enkindled but fears the reproach and censure of kith and kin - in the Qur'an it states "the blame of the blamer shall not delay them from God."
selected.reason: Addresses fear of communal reproach in a Sikh setting, preserving the particular interreligious context.

selected.text: although the situation is distressing now, I hope that in the future what was lost will be compensated and the means for organizing affairs will be provided. Verily with difficulty comes ease. This is a wave that has come - it has no permanence and will pass
selected.reason: Anticipates practical reorganization and compensation after a passing crisis.

selected.text: Praise must accord with reality and conduct, otherwise it becomes a test, placing the praised person under trial and tribulation, and God forbid that they should see any station or rank for themselves - then they would fall to the lowest depths of fire.
selected.reason: Identifies exaggerated praise itself as a test and requires praise to fit actual conduct.

selected.text: For some souls diseases and afflictions are the requital of actions. For others, they are the cause of awakening, so that they no longer attach their hearts to this evanescent world. In this case, hardships and tribulations are a gift.
selected.reason: Distinguishes different relationships of disease, actions and awakening rather than making one universal claim.

selected.text: Although tests and trials are decreasing in one respect, since day by day the banner of God's Cause waves more strongly and rises higher, yet in another respect hidden tests are clearly evident.
selected.reason: Recognizes hidden tests continuing while outward persecution diminishes.

selected.text: Know verily that calamities are of two kinds: one is a divine test of human beings; the other is retribution for one's own actions. The kind, which is meant as a test, is a form of training and discipline for the soul; and that which is retributive is a divine chastisement.
selected.reason: Explicitly distinguishes a trial from retribution for one's actions.

selected.text: Shouldst thou lament and cry, shouldst thou groan and complain, thou wouldst be justified for thou has sustained afflictions so continuous and calamities so great that no human being hath borne their like.
selected.reason: Validates complaint and lament under extraordinary suffering.

selected.text: For these thy prevailing diseases are not on account of sins, but they are to make thee detest this world and know that there is no rest and composure in this temporal life
selected.reason: Explicitly tells a recipient that their illness is not punishment for sins.

selected.text: The delay in answering the questions is because a detailed response was written to your honored father, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, but it is here [with me] and cannot be sent, as the safety of the route and peace and tranquility are uncertain
selected.reason: Explains withholding a written answer because the communication route is unsafe.

selected.text: They have fallen under the claws of fierce beasts of tribulations and dropped into the pit of abandonment through calamities. Drought and barrenness, illness and flood and woe have overcome that land and region, uprooting their foundations, shaking their pillars, sickening their bodies and distressing their spirits.
selected.reason: Describes drought, illness and abandonment together as concrete communal hardship.

selected.text: Praise be to God that in this severe test they were like a mountain of iron. It is hoped that these transgressions will come to an end.
selected.reason: Combines praise of endurance with an explicit hope that the transgressions will end.

selected.text: Wandering about and traveling long distances causes nervous and physical ailments
selected.reason: Recognizes nervous and physical consequences of prolonged travel and wandering.

selected.text: In this bloody war thou didst find solace and showed patience and forbearance. If there be no spiritual consolation, through what shall man find solace in the difficulties and pains of these days?
selected.reason: Asks how spiritual consolation sustains people amid a bloody war.

selected.text: It is the law of human life, that man must struggle with his tools for growth until he learns how to use them aright and to the best advantage. The Glory of God is known to man in that personal volition and responsibility is bestowed upon him as God's greatest gift in this Day of Maturity.
selected.reason: Frames human struggle through learning to use capacities responsibly in a reported account.

selected.text: The storm did not come to sink the ship but to follow its own natural course. Now, the more substantial and sturdy the ship, the better it can endure the force of the storm. Tests of the world of nature are of the same kind
selected.reason: Explains a storm through natural causation rather than an intention to sink a particular ship.

selected.text: It is incumbent upon us to deal with them in truth and love. Some are bad in character, they are not truthful, they bring false charges and I must satisfy all. How difficult is this task. It is very difficult!
selected.reason: Acknowledges the practical difficulty of answering false charges with truth and love.

selected.text: Whatever task God places before humans, He surely gives them the strength for it
selected.reason: Relates assigned responsibility to the strength needed to fulfill it in a reported saying.

selected.text: Tests are of various kinds, meeting the needs of the soul. Tests are not sent as punishment, but in reality to reveal the soul to itself. Tests reveal strength as well as weakness and provide opportunity to remedy defects.
selected.reason: Defines tests as revealing strength and weakness to the soul and enabling improvement.

selected.text: What hardship these coal miners have to suffer, how poor and needy they are!
selected.reason: Directs compassionate attention to poverty and hardship among coal miners.

selected.text: There are two kinds of suffering, one subtle, the other gross. The subtle suffering is hatred, anger, fear, and torment which follow evil actions of the soul. The gross suffering is imprisonment, chastisement, and physical pain of martyrdom.
selected.reason: Distinguishes inward moral suffering from physical suffering in a reported saying.

selected.text: Everything in life ministers to our development. Our lesson is to study and learn. Money and difficulties are alike advantages to us. Tests are either stumbling blocks or stepping-stones, just as
selected.reason: Treats both money and difficulty as occasions for learning, with outcomes depending on response.

selected.text: In truth, such objections have forever emanated from the people of hatred and rancor in the days of Divine Manifestation. However, this evanescent servant beseeches from the ocean of God's bounty and generosity that He may guide him and not deprive him of the breathings of revelation. It is human nature to err and make mistakes, while it is divine nature to forgive and bestow. We hope that with the arm of trust in God he may rend asunder the veils of idle fancies and vain imaginings and turn toward the Dawning-Place of certitude. Today is the day of return and the day of forgiveness and favor.
selected.reason: Pairs recognition of hostility with an invitation to return and receive forgiveness.

selected.text: In his loss there is profit, and in his harm there is benefit. We beseech God to make this very loss the essence of blessing and bounty. Verily, He is powerful over all things. O Afnan! Thou hast been and art with Us. Whatever befalleth, We are partners therein. Verily, He Who hath taken no partner unto Himself is God. We beseech Him to change hardship into ease, and difficulty into comfort.
selected.reason: Prays specifically for hardship to become ease and loss to become benefit.

selected.text: The tests and trials are discriminating angels of God who are occupied with separation and gathering - this is the meaning of what was revealed aforetime: "By those who drag forth violently." The intent is those discriminating angels who are charged with drawing forth and removing garments and spirits until distinction and separation become clear and evident
selected.reason: Interprets the scriptural image of separating angels through the discriminating work of tests.

selected.text: Be not grieved by hardship, for all are in hardship. And be not distressed by constraints, for all are under constraints. If there be no constraint of wealth, there must needs be constraint of aspirations. And if through the grace of the Beloved Who never fails the constraint of aspirations be removed, the constraint of greed remains.
selected.reason: Shows that constraints can persist through wealth, aspiration and greed as well as poverty.

selected.text: Know thou that We have heard that thy father hath cast thee out from the house because thou hast believed in God, the Almighty, the Most Noble. Grieve not at this, but rather be glad within thyself
selected.reason: Addresses expulsion from the family home for belief, preserving a concrete personal trial.

selected.text: O stranger in foreign lands! God willing, may this exile become the cause and means of comfort for steadfast and assured souls in the homeland. Many times exile leads to finding a homeland, and many are the homelands whose dust of exile is more excellent and beloved in God's sight. Exile in the path of the Friend is more beloved and precious to lovers than their homeland.
selected.reason: Connects one person's exile with possible comfort and benefit for others at home.

selected.text: By Thy glory, O my God! I have reached such a state of abasement that I have become hopeless of the breezes of Thy mercy, and have attained to such a degree of poverty that I see myself deprived of the fragrances of Thy glory
selected.reason: Gives voice to profound desolation within prayer rather than excluding it from devotion.

selected.text: After every hardship comes ease, after every distress comes tranquility
selected.reason: States succinctly the recurring transition from hardship toward tranquility.

selected.text: By God, the True One! The heavens wept and the earth lamented, and the hearts of existence were consumed. Such grief and sorrow, such tribulation and affliction descended from the clouds of divine decree that all the members of the household are now ill
selected.reason: Records grief affecting the health of an entire household.

selected.text: Yet at times doubts seize me and return me to the abode of the doubtful ones
selected.reason: Acknowledges the recurrence of doubt, requiring its exact prayerful setting.

selected.text: Here before Thy face I have brought my frame, my body, my form, my sight, my hearing, my spirit and my heart, and I desire to entrust them into the hands of Thy loving-kindness
selected.reason: Offers a whole-person prayer of entrusting body, senses, heart and spirit to loving-kindness.

selected.text: Every gathering has its dispersion, every union its separation, and every nearness is followed by remoteness. Such is the decree of the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
selected.reason: Places separation and reunion within the changing conditions of earthly life.

selected.text: It is evident that the nobler the aim and the higher the aspiration, the more difficult the path to its attainment. "Did ye think that ye would enter Paradise while yet there had not come unto you the like of what came to those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them." Likewise He says: "Ye will not attain it save with great difficulty." Furthermore, by Him besides Whom there is no God, tribulations and trials in the path of the Beloved of the horizons are the delight of those who drink the cup of bounty from the hand of the Cup-bearer of Oneness. The Bab--may the life of the worlds be sacrificed for Him--declares: "O my God! Were it not for trials and tribulations in Thy path, life and existence would hold no sweetness for me."
selected.reason: Relates the difficulty of a path to the nobility of its aim through a substantive explanation.

selected.text: How mighty, O my God, is the ordained fate, and how difficult for him is every inevitable decree! No skin is left on his body, no patience in his heart, no endurance in his soul. Nevertheless, he has naught save submission to Thy decree and contentment with Thy good-pleasure, though his patience be exhausted, his tears flowing, his heart aflame.
selected.reason: Describes exhausted patience and bodily suffering without denying continuing prayer.

selected.text: In recent years, calamities, trials and afflictions, both hidden and manifest, have encompassed the entire world. Yet praise be to God, the friends of God were to such a degree safe and secure, not suffering tribulations and trials like others.
selected.reason: Recognizes the friends' relative safety amid wider suffering, resisting claims of exclusive hardship.

selected.text: O ye faithful friends in this world neither wrong doing remaineth nor torment nor suffering, neither does comfort, rest, happiness, neither injury nor hurt--all will pass away, but those who suffer in the path of Baha will attain the great bounty. Others will be afflicted with manifest loss.
selected.reason: Treats comfort and affliction alike as transient while asking what endures.

selected.text: Although due to the calamities that have befallen and the successive afflictions, surely the pure water of the heart becomes clouded and the glass of the inner heart shatters, yet since it is in the path of the Beloved of the horizons, there is no harm in it. In this station, sorrows are harbingers of joy, and calamities and afflictions are heralds of delight and gladness. … Such tests have ever descended like torrential rain upon the friends of God
selected.reason: Acknowledges that repeated calamities can cloud the heart rather than automatically strengthen it.

selected.text: Without doubt, until snow and rain and cold and storms and severe blizzards occur, the capacity for spring is not prepared. In winter, the Lord makes preparation for life-giving spring. … Likewise, this severe war caused souls to awaken
selected.reason: Relates wartime suffering to awakening a desire for universal peace, preserving its historical frame.

selected.text: These afflictions are indeed beyond human endurance, yet from another perspective they are a divine bounty, for days pass and eventually come to an end in any case.
selected.reason: Acknowledges afflictions as beyond human endurance while presenting a spiritual perspective.

selected.text: Although physical trials pour down like heavenly rain, or rather like mountain torrents, yet the remembrance of the faces of the friends remains fixed and imprinted in my heart and soul
selected.reason: Shows remembrance of friends persisting through intense personal trials.

selected.text: For some time, due to poor health and physical weakness, I have been unable to write or speak. Letters from you and all the friends from various places remained unanswered, and I was very affected by this
selected.reason: Acknowledges inability to write or speak because of ill health and concern over unanswered letters.

selected.text: through the burning of the fire of test and persecution, was in great fear and denied Christ three times … committed against Him that which made the hearts lament, distressed the minds, caused tears to flow and the foundations of existence to tremble and shake
selected.reason: Examines Peter's denial under fear, providing a concrete case of failure under testing.

selected.text: Rather, one should fear and dread the severity of divine tests, lest any soul's flame of the love of God be extinguished and grow cold. This is cause for regret and occasion for remorse.
selected.reason: Identifies loss of love and spiritual coldness as a danger worth fearing.

selected.text: These were divine tests, for it is impossible for a person not to become the target of the arrow of destiny in this dustheap. Everyone suffers tribulations according to their capacity
selected.reason: Relates individual trials to capacity in a concise direct statement.

selected.text: Although the upheaval in Iran is severe and trials and tribulations have overcome everyone near and far, all parties are impatient and restless, each group is overwhelmed with grief and sorrow, blood has been spilled and homes have fallen, property has been plundered and pillaged, and leaders have become homeless
selected.reason: Situates community suffering within turmoil affecting all parties in Iran.

selected.text: So that man may be free of any attachment, detached from heedlessness, attracted by Divine love, sanctify his heart, possess a mature mind and be endowed with perfections, and distinguish between truth and error.
selected.reason: States the aims of detachment, mature judgment and distinguishing truth from error.

selected.text: However much they strive and agitate and seek to do battle, their efforts are brought to naught. They are disappointed and hopeless, for the real existence of the friends of God is safeguarded within the sanctuary of God's inviolable protection. Whatever cruelties they inflict affect the body only, not the soul; they touch the elements, not the mind.
selected.reason: Distinguishes bodily harm from the soul in explaining the limits of persecution.

selected.text: His Holiness Job fell into the most great divine tests, but he engaged in patience and forbearance. He endured all calamities and pains
selected.reason: Uses Job's endurance as a direct scriptural example of patient faithfulness.

selected.text: When his holiness Jonah became the companion of the whale in its belly and in infinite confinement, he cried out and sighed. He was patient, showed forbearance, repented and turned to God
selected.reason: Pairs Jonah's confinement with repentance, crying out and turning toward God.

selected.text: They withstood severe shocks and faced tribulations with smiling faces, throbbing hearts, and flowing tears. They thanked You when calamities befell them in Your path and difficulties surrounded them in Your love.
selected.reason: Presents smiling faces and flowing tears together, preserving emotional complexity.

selected.text: One must not look to the beginning of matters - one must strive in affairs with pure intention and ultimately await the results. Never has any fruit been produced from ease and comfort in any instance. Every result and fruit that has been produced in any age or century has come about through hardship and enduring difficulties and sacrificing one's life.
selected.reason: Calls for pure intention, sustained effort and judgment by outcomes rather than beginnings.

selected.text: Consider how souls of high resolve, whether earthly or heavenly, whether physical or spiritual, whether of the dust or of the celestial spheres, have always endured great hardships, and until they did so, they did not succeed.
selected.reason: Connects spiritual perseverance with the hardships of achievement in ordinary human pursuits.

selected.text: If there were no trials, patience would not be realized. If there were no disturbance, there would be no tranquility and composure. If there were no tribulations and pain, rest and comfort would not exist. If there were no sorrows, no one would be joyful.
selected.reason: Explains patience and composure through their relation to contrary experiences.

selected.text: Especially since this is the season of trials and the time of oppression. In such circumstances one must be warm, nay rather, gentle.
selected.reason: Explicitly requires gentleness during a season of oppression and trial.

selected.text: You endured endless hardship and bore boundless difficulties. Then you were commanded to return, which caused you much tribulation.
selected.reason: Acknowledges the pain of being asked to return after an arduous journey.

selected.text: Though from the descent of this dark, blind calamity the darkness of grief and sorrow hath encompassed the kingdom of being and reality itself desireth non-existence, yet we must arise to exalt the Word of God and afterwards hope for ascension.
selected.reason: Responds to devastating bereavement by directing attention toward continued service in life.

selected.text: For some time you have withdrawn to a corner of obscurity … if there is some temporary disruption in the continuation of your position and duties, this is due to the requirements of this faithless world and the manners of these shameless times
selected.reason: Addresses loss of duties and withdrawal, linking trials to disrupted livelihood.

selected.text: We had hoped that in these endless trials and tribulations the friends would become a healing balm for the wounds inflicted by the oppressors.
selected.reason: Calls on friends to heal wounds inflicted by oppressors through supportive fellowship.

selected.text: whatever wounds they inflict have become like honey, for they gladden the spirit and their impact is merely physical. But the lack of fellowship among the friends with one another is a spiritual wound, and it also causes the body to waste away from the severity of the spirit's distress.
selected.reason: Distinguishes outward wounds from the deeper distress caused by a lack of fellowship.

selected.text: Thou hast sustained many afflictions and diverse adversities. Thou hast borne the martyrdom of thy distinguished brother with patience and acquiescence.
selected.reason: Addresses grief after a brother's martyrdom and acknowledges patient bereavement.

selected.text: Truly you have endured much hardship and reached a state of weakness
selected.reason: Acknowledges that sustained hardship can lead to actual weakness.

selected.text: Though you are aged in body, yet in spirit you are a living youth … Especially in these days when you have gained freshness and grace through blows, strikes and slaps from the hands of oppressors in the path of God. This has become light upon light - you have become even fresher and more graceful
selected.reason: Contrasts bodily aging with renewed spiritual vitality after hardship.

selected.text: Although in the blessed Tablets this verse of Sana'i is written: "If He bestows the pearl of bounty, behold the hearts are its shells, and if the arrow of calamity comes, behold the souls are its targets," yet for you I wish the pearl of bounty, not the arrow of calamity.
selected.reason: Explicitly wishes bounty rather than calamity for the recipient despite the poetry of sacrifice.

selected.text: For faith and certitude without tests provide no assurance or reliability - they may vanish due to some minor matter or illusory doubts
selected.reason: Questions the reliability of confidence that has never faced a test.

selected.text: in the Holy Land there is no work or employment available and the tests are severe
selected.reason: Identifies unavailable employment as a concrete difficulty in the Holy Land.

selected.text: For at all times, avoidance of dangers, trials, and harmful perils taketh precedence, while the pursuit of benefits, glad-tidings, virtues and advantages cometh after.
selected.reason: Gives avoidance of dangerous and harmful conditions priority over pursuing benefits.

selected.text: The father and the teacher sometimes humor the children and then again discipline them. This discipline is for educational purposes and is indeed to give them true happiness; it is absolute kindness and true providence. Although in appearance it is wrath yet in reality it is kindness. Although outwardly it is an ordeal yet inwardly it is purifying water.
selected.reason: Uses parental and educational discipline as an analogy, requiring its complete qualifications.

selected.text: For the meaning of this name is "fierce lion" and its quality is boundless courage. But manliness lies not in ferocity, and courage consists not in force and might. … Rather, true manliness and wisdom lie in freedom from all save God. If, through divine strength, you gain deliverance from the clutches of the commanding self, you are indeed Rustam, son of Zal, and steadfast at the Divine Threshold
selected.reason: Distinguishes courage and manliness from ferocity and physical force.

selected.text: thou too hast received an abundant share and hast endured severe persecution from thy kindred and tribe. Although thy relatives provided protection from others, they themselves caused sufficient harm.
selected.reason: Recognizes that relatives can offer protection from outsiders while themselves causing harm.

selected.text: O Lord! These are servants enslaved; free their necks from chains and fetters
selected.reason: Prays expressly for captives to be freed from chains and fetters.

selected.text: In this prohibition [from visiting Haifa] there is a providence which will become manifest before long. But know ye with the utmost certainty that this disappointment is regarded in the Threshold of the Manifest Light as greater than a visit to that magnificent station. For the substance of the grief is the essence of the visit
selected.reason: Addresses disappointment at a historically prohibited visit to Haifa without making the restriction universal.

selected.text: Jacob's eyes turned white from grief, Job was afflicted with all manner of diseases and illnesses, yet their radiant reality remained pure and sanctified from every dust
selected.reason: Combines Jacob's grief and Job's illness with the continuing dignity of their spiritual reality.

selected.text: Your noble father has forsaken home and country … You are truly counted among those who strive in the path of God, for you are always far and separated from him
selected.reason: Recognizes children's separation from a serving parent as participation in sacrifice.

selected.text: Thou seest and beholdest the dust that hath risen to the highest heaven, and the smoke that hath enveloped humanity, and the mist that hath spread from all directions. The whirlwind of doubts hath come, and the tornado of veils, and the storm of individual interpretation
selected.reason: Names uncontrolled individual interpretation as a source of confusion during testing.

selected.text: How I long to be far away from all the people for two months, somewhere where I have not to read letters, answer questions and always associate with men. Can you deliver me from all this work so that I may rest for awhile
selected.reason: Records a candid desire for rest from continual work and correspondence.

selected.text: The tremendous trials and besetting difficulties of the world-stage encircle them like unto a whirl-wind. Having not rehearsed their parts thoroughly and not being warned beforehand, they become bewildered, discouraged, scared and ere long you see them flowing back, back to their origin - the indistinct mass of humanity, staying there forever and never aspiring and preparing themselves for a second rise, a second attempt and a second examination.
selected.reason: Uses the stage and rehearsal to discuss recovering from failure and making another attempt.

selected.text: When Baha'u'llah in the early history of the Cause desired to test any one, he would say something contrary to his established opinion.
selected.reason: Describes attachment to established opinions as a test in a historical reported account.

selected.text: What a hard time I had often till midnight going through villages and trying to persuade the farmers to sell us something. Especially at that time there was a famine in those districts and people loathed to give up their hoarded provisions, fearing the worse may come also to them.
selected.reason: Shows the practical labor of obtaining food during famine and exile.

selected.text: But if a rich man be compassionate, he is very near to God, for he has come out of temptation.
selected.reason: Recognizes compassion in a wealthy person as overcoming the temptation of riches.

selected.text: We must not fear difficulties and labor. They lead us to the noblest end. We must resist the whole world, for the world wants war; unite our efforts and with divine love we will succeed.
selected.reason: Joins endurance of difficulty to united work against war.

selected.text: The friends of God must always strive so that in faith and assurance they may advance day after day; and that the tests may not cause their stagnation; for the cause of the stagnation is often the tests and trials of God.
selected.reason: Warns that tests can cause stagnation, so progress requires continuing effort.

selected.text: Once there was an official who in order to intimidate me to bribe him came one morning and said: 'I shall write inflammatory letters and throw them into the window into your house; then shall [I] send the police to search and seize these documents and thus you will be convicted.'
selected.reason: Records a concrete threat of fabricated evidence intended to extort a bribe.

selected.text: Should anyone at any time encounter hard and perplexing times, he must say to himself, "This will soon pass." Then he will be calm and quiet. In all my calamity and difficulties I used to say to myself, "This will pass away." Then I became patient.
selected.reason: Offers remembrance of change and impermanence as a practical response to distress.

selected.text: Inner troubles and afflictions increase day by day. Until now, I alone have endured and continue to endure them. This is not the time for martyrdom
selected.reason: Explicitly says this is not the time for martyrdom, preserving historical limits on sacrificial language.

selected.text: Otherwise, if a rabid dog confronts a person, he will perforce show submission and humility. When anyone encounters a tyrant, an oppressor, or a bloodthirsty one, he becomes submissive--but what benefit is there in this? How many souls were submissive and humble before Yazid, but out of fear--what benefit is there in this? It yields no result.
selected.reason: Distinguishes voluntary humility from submission produced merely by fear of a tyrant.

selected.text: By Thy might! It is as though I see this station of mine as the summit of Paradise, for whoever can praise Thee cares not for the displeasure of Thy servants, and whoever delights in intimacy with Thy presence misses no good in the presence of Thy Divine Dominion. Therefore, unto Thee be praise in this station of mine - a praise radiant, effulgent, luminous and sanctified, which excels all praise as Thy Self excels all Thou hast created, for Thou hast freed me on this mountain for Thy worship
selected.reason: Presents the Bab's mountain confinement as a setting for intimacy with God, preserving prayerful context.

selected.text: A group from Qazvin submits that if we deny this true Cause in our province, we may perhaps be able to remain with a thousand mockeries and taunts, otherwise they deem our death obligatory
selected.reason: Records coercive pressure on believers in Qazvin and the threat attached to religious identity.

selected.text: Thou art He Who ordaineth not any trial for anyone except that Thou hast ordained for him a reward through Thy grace and bounty. Therefore, pour forth upon him, O Lord, patience and deliver us from every affliction through Thy grace.
selected.reason: Joins reward and patience with a prayer for deliverance from affliction.

selected.text: And as for the rest of the blessed verse, it indicates the testing and trial in this world, for this world is the world of experience and testing, that the blessed may be distinguished from the wretched, light from darkness, and the misguided from the guided.
selected.reason: Explains the present world as a realm of experience and testing in scriptural interpretation.

selected.text: The flowing pen of that beloved of the heart somewhat consoled and brought solace to this grief-stricken heart from the oppression of the earth. Were it not for the gentle breezes of love for His loved ones, the heart would burst and existence would not be sustained.
selected.reason: Recognizes a friend's letter as real consolation that sustains a grief-stricken heart.

selected.text: Beware lest the utterances of the ignorant sadden you or the commands of the oppressors frighten you. Hold fast unto that which is good in all circumstances, and commit not that which would cause the clamor of the idolaters to be raised.
selected.reason: Pairs steadfast goodness with prudence about provoking hostile clamor.

selected.text: He hath once again been afflicted with trials. We beseech God first to adorn him with the ornament of patience, then to deliver him through His power and sovereignty.
selected.reason: Prays first for patience and then for actual deliverance through divine aid.

selected.text: O people! Mock not those who have been afflicted with trials in God's path. These are among the most exalted of creation, and through them doth mercy descend upon the peoples of the world, were ye but to know.
selected.reason: Explicitly forbids mocking people afflicted in God's path.

selected.text:
Such is the
tale of this Youth and such are the circumstances surrounding Him on all
sides as a result of that which hath been perpetrated by the hands of them
for whose protection We have made Our bosom a shield, that the darts
of the envious may not touch them
selected.reason: Portrays shielding others from harm as a purpose of accepting suffering oneself.

selected.text: God will test you with a river - whoso draweth nigh unto it is not of the truth, and whoso turneth away from it is verily of the people of eternity
selected.reason: Uses the scriptural river trial to explore restraint and discernment rather than physical endurance alone.

selected.text: Despite all this, and griefs the like of which have never appeared in the world, the Most Exalted Pen moves and the Tongue speaks.
selected.reason: Shows ongoing writing and utterance amid otherwise inexpressible grief.

selected.text: of causative manifestations, I reveal to all the worlds the concealed tyranny of the excluded oppressor. Through the means of wealth I distinguish between generosity and miserliness, and through the means of deeds I make evident knowledge
selected.reason: Explains wealth and deeds as concrete means of revealing generosity, miserliness and knowledge.

selected.text: We previously informed the people about the days of adversity, lest they be disturbed when the winds of trials blow from the direction of the All-Merciful. Thus was the decree ordained in the Tablet. And when they blew, souls were disturbed, but God pardoned them
selected.reason: Records pardon for souls disturbed by trials despite earlier warnings.

selected.text: Your pilgrimage is accepted, but your effort is not appreciated, for in such days as these, beholding the oppressed and wandering ones has incalculable reward and is in truth the robe of deeds and the crown of actions
selected.reason: Gives visiting the oppressed and displaced a distinctive place among valued actions.

selected.text: Nothing shall befall us except what God has ordained for us. Were it not for the glad-tidings "Give thou good news unto the patient ones," the threats of "We shall surely prove you with somewhat of fear" would have transported the servants from existence to non-existence, just as He brought them from non-existence into being.
selected.reason: Connects scriptural warnings about testing with sustaining glad tidings for the patient.

selected.text: We have chosen tribulations for the reformation of the world and the unity of all therein
selected.reason: States the reformation and unity of the world as the purpose of accepted tribulation.

selected.text: All who dwell on earth today have been tested by the blessed Word that has dawned from the horizon of the merciful Will. Some, following their desires, remained veiled from the Lord of all beings, while others turned with utmost longing and yearning toward the divine horizon of manifestation.
selected.reason: Identifies response to the revealed Word as a test of recognition and desire.

selected.text: Yet it is observed that some become disturbed by certain words of others and by the rejection or acceptance of souls.
selected.reason: Examines vulnerability to other people's acceptance and rejection.

selected.text: And the glory rest upon thee and upon those whom God hath preserved through His sovereignty and delivered from the depths of trials
selected.reason: Gives thanks for preservation and deliverance from the depths of trials.

selected.text: How many a ruler hath been prevented from attaining the presence of the Countenance, and how many a poor one hath attained and said: "Praise be unto Thee, O Thou Goal of them that know!"
selected.reason: Contrasts worldly rank with recognition, showing that rulers may miss what poor people attain.

selected.text: O friends! The touchstone in your midst distinguisheth the truthful from the false. Mere claims were not and are not sufficient.
selected.reason: States plainly that verbal claims alone do not establish truthfulness.

selected.text: To whatever extent they can maintain outward appearances, it is permissible and acceptable. That is, if it is possible to return home in utmost joy and fragrance, that would be best. Otherwise, let not grief enter your noble being, and be exceedingly happy that you have migrated to God and journeyed unto Him.
selected.reason: Addresses a possible return home and outward conduct under particular historical conditions.

selected.text: for it is not known which souls have been elevated to the highest heaven by the fragrances of trials wafting from the right hand of the Will of the All-Merciful, and which have been cast down to the lowest depths
selected.reason: Acknowledges uncertainty about other souls' outcomes under testing, limiting confident judgment.

selected.text: Those souls who considered themselves the most learned, distinguished and accomplished were not and are not mentioned in the presence of God. By the life of God! If the veil were lifted, those who turned away would circle around those who turned towards God, and would flock from all directions to attain their presence and meeting. However, consummate wisdom has concealed this, so that there might be manifested from them in His days what was hidden within them and stored in their inmost beings.
selected.reason: Questions self-assumed learning and distinction when inward realities become apparent.

selected.text: O my Lord! Pour forth upon me patience in my exile from this severe cold
selected.reason: Prays for patience amid the specific bodily hardship of severe cold in exile.

selected.text: How many a worker hath been prevented today from attaining the presence of his Lord, though created for that purpose, and how many a heedless one hath attained and been numbered among the successful!
selected.reason: Allows for unexpected recognition by the previously heedless and failure by the outwardly active.

selected.text: This is a year of hardship for the servants and a year of divine decree for Us. If aught befalleth Us, We are supremely content, and if it be averted, We are supremely thankful.
selected.reason: Balances contentment if hardship arrives with gratitude when it is averted.

selected.text: Strive thou within thyself, then struggle in thine own being, lest anything prevent thee from the love of thy Lord, for in these days the breezes of temptation have blown from the direction of tests, causing leaves to fall even as the autumn winds cause them to fall - thus hath the Cause been known in truth.
selected.reason: Directs struggle inward toward one's own attachments and susceptibility.

selected.text: In every Revelation, He revealeth the essence of that Revelation in a manner contrary to the understanding and desires of men, and this very contrariness is the standard and the path of His Cause, and the source of tests and trials. Even as was witnessed in the Revelation of the Year Sixty, when the Promised Beauty appeared in a way contrary to all that the people possessed, whereupon such a clamor arose among the servants that every learned one fell, every illumined one was darkened, and every exalted one was brought low--all these conditions being witnessed with manifest evidence.
selected.reason: Explains revelation contrary to accustomed expectations as a central form of testing.

selected.reference: LG#944 (29 May 1935 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: As long as there will be life on earth, there will also be suffering, in various forms and degrees. But suffering, although an inescapable reality, can nevertheless be utilized as a means for the attainment of happiness. This is the interpretation given to it by all the Prophets and saints, who, in the midst of severe tests and trials, felt happy and joyous and experienced what is best and holiest in life. Suffering is both a reminder and a guide. It stimulates us to better adapt ourselves to our environmental conditions, and thus leads the way to self-improvement. In every suffering one can find a meaning and a wisdom. It is sometimes only when all our suffering has passed that we become aware of its usefulness. What man considers to be evil turns often to be a cause of infinite blessings. And this is due to his desire to know more than he can. God's wisdom is, indeed, inscrutable to us all, and it is no use pushing too far trying to discover that which shall always remain a mystery to our mind.

selected.reference: COC#1334 (6 Oct. 1954 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: Naturally there will be periods of distress and difficulty, and even severe tests; but if that person turns firmly toward the divine Manifestation, studies carefully His spiritual teachings and receives the blessings of the Holy Spirit, he will find that in reality these tests and difficulties have been the gifts of God to enable him to grow and develop. selected.text: O friends of God and maidservants of the Most Merciful! Your detailed letter was an extensive statement about steadfastness and firmness. Although in these days full of tests, steadfastness and firmness were difficult, yet praise be to God, the friends of God and maidservants of the Most Merciful remained firm and steadfast like a mighty rock - rather, they increased in their steadfastness. This is the custom and the way: in the day of tests, the weak become completely shaken and turn away, while the strong who possess spiritual power increase in strength.
